A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same federated model-evaluation framework despite the changed title and organization. Their text, equations, figures, and complete appendices support comparison: Appendices A–E in v1 and A–G in v2.

before.justification: Section 7 and Appendix E report original federated simulations and certification results on CIFAR-10, SVHN, EMNIST, and ImageNet, including feature, label, resolution, color, and Wasserstein shifts.

after.justification: Section 8 and Appendix G report original simulations on the same four datasets, with revised client counts and certification curves.

M1.justification: The query framework, risk reweighting, and Wasserstein bisection procedure remain. However, the f-divergence optimization changes from weights between Lambda^-1 and Lambda to weights between zero and Lambda = 1 + kappa*epsilon, changing the feasible solutions in both mean-risk and CDF estimation.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same four datasets, feature/label/combined shifts, CIFAR-10 resolution and color shifts, and Wasserstein adversarial scenarios. Combined-shift panels omitted from v2's main figures remain in Appendix G; changed client counts do not introduce new coverage.

E2.justification: Reported comparator membership changes. The Meta100 empirical-CDF reference in v1 Figures 2/6 disappears from v2 Figures 4/9, which include an 'adv' curve. The full-population Wass reference and Meta100 curve in v1 Figures 5/7 are absent from v2 Figures 7/10. The precise construction of 'adv' is not explained.

E3.justification: The reported population increases from 500 to 1000 clients, and the main-text observed/unseen split changes from 100/400 to 500/500, retaining 1000 samples per client. Divergence budgets also change, including both budgets becoming 0.2 throughout v2 Figure 9. Appendix G.1 nevertheless retains the old 100/400 description, leaving the implemented split inconsistent.

E4.justification: Existing budget-sensitivity and certificate-tightness analyses are revised. For resolution and color shifts, v1 Figure 4 displays two certificate budgets per divergence, whereas v2 Figure 6 displays one alongside an 'adv' curve. The four-dataset robustness analyses and exploratory Wasserstein-CDF evaluation remain; no new component-ablation study appears.

E5.justification: V1's empirical plots contain shaded bands that disappear in v2, but their statistical meaning and construction are insufficiently specified to distinguish uncertainty reporting from certificate visualization. Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run counts, or a clearly defined empirical confidence-interval procedure.

E6.justification: Certification results are substantially revised across the main and appendix plots, with changed CDF curves, added 'adv' results, and removed sampled-CDF and full-population Wasserstein references. For example, the chi-square/KL curve ordering differs between the CIFAR-10 label-shift panels of v1 Figure 6 and v2 Figure 9. Changed populations and divergence budgets prevent interpreting these replacements as same-setting performance improvements.

T1.justification: V2 removes v1's explicit two-sided density-ratio assumption and restricted f-divergence ball, replacing them with a claimed derived cap in Appendix D, equations (59)–(60). Appendix F adds detailed asymptotic optimality arguments for all four main theorems and a client-side optimization derivation. The robust DKW/Glivenko–Cantelli results themselves largely move to Appendix B rather than being newly introduced.

C1.justification: V2's Introduction broadens the novelty claim to the absence of prior theoretical bounds for meta-distributionally robust federated evaluation or beta testing; v1 emphasized the first robust DKW/Glivenko–Cantelli extension. The central certification, efficiency, and vanishing-gap claims remain. Minimax optimality becomes prominent in the abstract but was already asserted in v1 Remark 5.5 and Appendix E.

C2.justification: V2 Remark 7.3 explicitly excludes differential-privacy certificates and identifies reconstruction attacks and information-theoretic privacy analysis as future work, qualifying v1's privacy discussion. The Impact Statement also cautions against applying certificates without validating shift assumptions. Both versions retain the limitation that Wasserstein-CDF guarantees are explored empirically rather than proved.

D1.justification: V2 adds a project-code link and expands the client-side dual-optimization and SGD explanation in Appendix F. Section 8.1 specifies a CNN where v1 only specified a DNN, providing additional model-type information without establishing an architecture change. Detailed training hyperparameters and hardware remain undocumented.

R1.justification: V2 substantially expands research positioning through Appendix A and the rewritten Introduction. New discussion covers federated evaluation and beta testing, meta-distribution models, superquantile aggregation, and MMD-based alternatives with non-vanishing gaps. Added references include Soltani et al., Pillutla et al., and Hu et al.; this extends considerably beyond relocating v1's related-work section.

P1.justification: The title and Introduction are substantially rewritten around robust federated evaluation and beta testing. Related work moves to Appendix A, ordinary-risk theorems are consolidated, DKW material moves to Appendix B, and computational/privacy/optimality remarks are collected into Section 7. Experimental explanations are redistributed between the main text and Appendix G.

P2.justification: V2 adopts a two-column conference layout for the main text, adds three explanatory diagrams, and relocates v1 Figure 1 to Appendix Figure 8. Main experimental grids are reduced from six to four panels while full coverage remains in the appendix. Numerous plots change legends, colors, reference curves, and shading; Algorithm 1 is reformatted.

improvement.justification: V2 improves exposition, expands optimality arguments, and documents code access, but introduces a substantive correctness regression in central guarantees. V1 explicitly assumes bounded density ratios; v2 removes that restriction while Appendix D, equations (59)–(60), incorrectly infers a uniform ratio cap from bounded f-divergence. Bounded chi-square divergence permits arbitrarily large ratios on rare client types, so the capped estimator need not bound the newly claimed worst case even asymptotically. This undermines a central certification result and outweighs the presentation gains.
